title: Research-run References get junk titles, raw URLs and reasons that say nothing
description:
Found on the 18 References the Machines on Machines research assignment linked to its Story, 2026-11-03.

- Titles copied from search results: '[2204.06974] Planting Undetectable Backdoorsin Machine ...', 'seL4 | Proceedings of the 2013 IEEE Symposium on Security and ...', 'Language-Based Information-Flow Security - CS@Cornell', 'Theory of Computer Science' (a course handout).
- Session junk kept in the address: link.springer.com/...?error=cookies_not_supported&code=<uuid>, which also defeats URL dedupe.
- Mirrors instead of the record: ar5iv rather than arXiv, a personal copy rather than the DOI. The direction asked for primary sources, but Rice's theorem is Wikipedia and a slide handout.
- The context pack shows 'Accepted because: Found by perplexity (undecidability proof)': a search provider's name as an editorial reason.
- The Confused Deputy shows 'Accepted because: This doesn't seem to relate to AI/ML or be a computing principle that generalizes', which reads as a reason for rejecting it. I have not confirmed its stored status; whichever it is, the label is wrong.

Expected: clean the title and URL, prefer the canonical record, keep a discovery note apart from an accept reason. Related: PPY-24fdf4, PPY-f8ff49.
